title: Python C-ABI — install and Dense forward
why: Use the same Welvet engine from Python via ctypes over a prebuilt C ABI — no Go toolchain required for day-to-day scripts.
what: Install welvet==1.1.2, assert the CABI contract, create a CPU grid, place a Dense layer, and run one forward.
body_extra:
Package vs engine

Python package / CABI contract is 1.1.2. The Go engine behind the shared library is Welvet v1.7.3. Wheels ship the matching welvet.so / welvet.dylib (Linux x86_64 manylinux includes CUDA/ROCm/Vulkan/cpp siblings; macOS arm64 includes Metal).

pip install welvet==1.1.2

Replaces the Loom-era PyPI line (welvet==0.80.0). Prefer create_grid + place_* over legacy Loom network helpers. Sibling docs: w2a/python/README.md. Backends: §115. Train + entity: §116. Layers: §117.

title: Python C-ABI — list backends and pick one
why: Accelerators are opt-in at runtime. Scripts should probe what this host can run instead of hard-coding CUDA or Metal.
what: Print list_backends(), then create a grid on the first available accelerator (or CPU), place Dense, and forward once.
body_extra:
Backend ids

cpu_tiled · simd · webgpu · native_cpu · cuda · metal · rocm · vulkan · qnn · mlx. Routed GPU backends enable Go EnableRouting inside the CABI. For qnn / mlx, call prepare_grid after place_* (SyncTo* before forward) — see §117.

Missing sibling libs or no GPU print as available: false; create_grid with an unavailable name raises. Prefer probe → pick → place. Go twins: §89 CUDA · §82 Metal · §110 MLX.

title: Python C-ABI — train SGD and .entity round-trip
why: Training and checkpoints should match the Go ENTITY path so Python scripts can hand off to Go apps (and back).
what: Train one Dense step with train_sgd, serialize to .entity bytes, deserialize a second grid, and free both handles.
body_extra:
Checkpoint bytes

serialize_entity returns the same Welvet .entity blob the Go engine writes. deserialize_entity returns a new grid handle — always free_grid both. For cameral / named train modes see Go book §67 and Python list_named_train_modes() / train_stack_mse.

Requirements: chapter 114.

title: Python C-ABI — MHA place and prepare_grid
why: Not every layer is Dense. Python place takes the same kind strings as Go; some accelerators need an explicit prepare/Sync before forward.
what: Place an MHA layer with a shaped forward, list layer kinds, and show the prepare_grid call used for qnn/mlx mounts.
body_extra:
place kinds

place(handle, kind, spec) accepts Dense, Softmax, RMSNorm, LayerNorm, MHA, SwiGLU, CNN*, LSTM, Embedding, Residual, Sequential, and friends — see list_layer_types(). Shaped tensors use the shape= argument on forward.

prepare_grid runs SyncTo* for backends that need an explicit mount (notably qnn / mlx). Routed CUDA/Metal/ROCm/Vulkan usually do not need it after create_grid(backend=…). Release assets: GitHub cabi-v1.1.2 · PyPI welvet==1.1.2.
